intro01.why: Every program needs a first observable result.
intro01.learn: Rove allows top-level code, and a function can be called explicitly.
intro01.task: Run the starter program, then change the greeting and run it again.
intro01.expected: A greeting appears in the terminal.

intro02.why: A compiler can only understand complete source expressions.
intro02.learn: String literals must begin and end with the same quote character.
intro02.task: Read the diagnostic, find the unmatched quote, and repair the print call.
intro02.expected: The program compiles and prints one complete sentence.

variables01.why: Names make values readable and let the compiler check your intent.
variables01.learn: `let` creates an immutable binding; its value cannot be reassigned.
variables01.task: Declare `x` with the value 42, then inspect the existing output.

variables02.why: Some state changes during a program, such as a score or counter.
variables02.learn: Use `var` for mutable state and `set` for an explicit update.
variables02.task: Change the binding to mutable and keep the update legal.
variables02.expected: The counter changes without a const or immutable-binding error.

variables05.why: Programs become useful when they calculate values from input data.
variables05.learn: Expressions can combine typed bindings with arithmetic operators.
variables05.task: Calculate the rectangle area from the existing width and height.
variables05.expected: The calculated area is printed instead of a hard-coded number.

types01.why: Static types catch incorrect assumptions before the program runs.
types01.learn: A decimal value belongs to `float`, while a whole-number value belongs to `int`.
types01.task: Make the annotation match the decimal value and read the diagnostic carefully.
types01.expected: The file passes the type checker.

functions01.why: A named operation can be reused instead of copied.
functions01.learn: `fn` defines a function; its body runs when the function is called.
functions01.task: Define `call_me` and call it from the existing program.
functions01.expected: The message is printed once by the function.

functions02.why: Typed function boundaries document what goes in and comes out.
functions02.learn: Parameters receive values and `-> int` declares the return type.
functions02.task: Complete the multiplication function without changing its contract.
functions02.expected: The caller receives the product as an integer.

if01.why: A program needs to choose a response based on its data.
if01.learn: `if`, `elif`, and `else` select one branch in order.
if01.task: Complete the temperature decision and test more than one value.
if01.expected: The correct message is selected for each temperature range.

loops01.why: Repetition is clearer and safer when the range is explicit.
loops01.learn: `for i in 1..5` visits an inclusive numeric range in Rove.
loops01.task: Sum the numbers in the range and print the accumulated result.

loops02.why: Some loops continue until state reaches a condition.
loops02.learn: A `while` loop checks its condition before each iteration.
loops02.task: Update the counter so the countdown reaches zero and terminates.
loops02.expected: The output counts down to 0 without an infinite loop.

match01.why: Many branches become easier to read when they describe values directly.
match01.learn: `match` selects an arm, and `_` provides a required fallback.
match01.task: Add the fallback arm and decide what unknown input should produce.
match01.expected: Known input matches its arm and unknown input is handled safely.

arrays01.why: Real programs usually process a collection rather than one value.
arrays01.learn: Array indexes start at zero and return an element of the array type.
arrays01.task: Read the second inventory item using its zero-based index.

arrays03.why: Aggregating a collection is a common pattern in applications.
arrays03.learn: A loop can maintain an accumulator while visiting each array element.
arrays03.task: Add every number in the array to the existing sum variable.
arrays03.expected: The printed sum equals the sum of all elements.

structs01.why: A domain object should keep related fields together.
structs01.learn: A `struct` defines named fields and a value can be created from it.
structs01.task: Declare the `Point` shape and construct the point used by the program.
structs01.expected: The point's fields can be accessed by name.

structs02.why: Behavior belonging to a data type should live near that type.
structs02.learn: An `impl` block adds methods; `self` refers to the current value.
structs02.task: Add `self` to the method signature and return the calculated area.
structs02.expected: Calling the method uses the struct's own fields.

enums01.why: A value with a small fixed set of states should not be a magic number.
enums01.learn: An `enum` names its allowed variants and makes state readable.
enums01.task: Declare `Status` with the three variants used by the program.
enums01.expected: The program can refer to `Status.Idle`, `Running`, and `Stopped`.

errors01.why: Recoverable failures should be handled instead of crashing silently.
errors01.learn: `try` runs fallible code and `catch` handles a thrown error.
errors01.task: Catch the validation error and print the required fallback message.
errors01.expected: The error is handled and the program continues normally.

null01.why: Missing data is normal in user input and external systems.
null01.learn: `string?` can contain a string or `null`; `??` supplies a fallback.
null01.task: Use the fallback name when the nickname is absent.
null01.expected: The program prints `Guest` for a null nickname.

result02.why: A domain failure is data that a caller may want to recover from.
result02.task: Return `Err` for division by zero and `Ok` for valid input.
result02.expected: Both success and failure paths are represented explicitly.

result03.why: Nested failure checks become noisy in a multi-step operation.
result03.learn: Postfix `?` returns an error from the current function when needed.
result03.task: Propagate the source error with `?` instead of repeating a manual branch.
result03.expected: The caller receives the original typed error unchanged.

pipeline01.why: A readable data flow makes transformations easier to inspect.
pipeline01.learn: `|>` passes one result into the next function.
pipeline01.task: Connect the increment and doubling functions in the given order.
pipeline01.expected: The value is transformed once by each stage.

defer01.why: Resources must be cleaned up even when work exits early.
defer01.learn: `defer` schedules a call for scope exit.
defer01.task: Register the lock release before doing the critical work.
defer01.expected: Cleanup runs when the function returns.

modules01.why: A growing program needs boundaries between reusable pieces.
modules01.learn: `import` selects functionality from another module or standard library package.
modules01.task: Import `sin` and `cos`, then combine their values at angle zero.
modules01.expected: The module functions are available without copying their implementation.

quiz01.why: A capstone proves that features work together in a real domain.
quiz01.learn: This project combines structs, methods, arrays, loops, match, and guards.
quiz01.task: Finish the inventory score calculator, then add one item of your own.
quiz01.expected: The final score is calculated from the inventory data, not hard-coded.
